name: @spsm/website
description: Public parish website. Static export to Firebase Hosting.

scripts.//dev: No --port flag on purpose. Next honours $PORT and otherwise takes 3000, stepping up if it is busy — so this coexists with whatever else is already running instead of failing to start.
scripts.//dev:https: HTTPS on :3000 with a self-signed certificate. Needed to fill a card: browsers only offer saved payment methods on a secure origin, and Square's own iframe wants one too. First run installs a local CA and will ask for your password.
scripts.//dev:emulated: The website against an already-running emulator suite, on the usual port. This is what makes the program galleries developable: they read Firestore in the browser, and the real project has no gallery data. Start the emulators first (npm run emulators) and seed them (npm run seed:emulator).
scripts.//dev:emulated:second: The same, alongside a server you already have running. `next dev` refuses a second server for the same output directory, so this one gets its own (.next-emulated, gitignored) and its own port. Use it to compare the real Firestore and the emulators side by side without stopping either.
scripts.//dev:emulated:third: A third server, for when :3100 is already taken by another session working in this same tree. Its own output directory again — `next dev` refuses two servers sharing one.

//firebase-admin: A devDependency, not a dependency: it is used only by src/features/bulletin/data.ts, which runs during `next build` to read the announcements project with its service-account key. Nothing it touches reaches the browser, and the static export ships no server code at all.
